target_customer: Consumers hunting for daily deals, monetised through deal referrals (monetisation not documented)
problem: Daily deal sites flooded users with offers (deal fatigue), so finding a relevant deal required scanning many emails and sites.
business_model: Deal search and ranking aggregator, likely affiliate referral fees (not confirmed by a source)

founders.name: Sanjay Mavinkurve
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch describes both founders as former Google engineers.

competitors.name: Yipit
competitors.what: Daily deal aggregator described as Kayak for daily deals

competitors.name: The Dealmap
competitors.funding_then: Acquired by Google (per Cornell profile page, not read in detail)

competitors.name: Dealhomer
competitors.what: Collected daily deals from over 150 sites

technical_complexity.rationale: Crawling and normalising deals from many sites plus a patent-pending ranking system called DealRank (per TechCrunch) is moderate engineering for a two-person team.

defensibility.rationale: Aggregation of public deal feeds was copyable and several aggregators already existed; the ranking claim was the only differentiator and no traction evidence exists.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google already owned a deal search product by 2010; the daily deal category itself contracted after 2012. No source shows any incumbent acting against Zipio specifically.

market_need_then: Daily deal volume exploded in 2010 and 2011 and TechCrunch described deal fatigue in early 2012, so a filter had some demand, but the sources show no usage numbers.

branding.domain_note: Product used dealupa.com while the YC directory lists the company as Zipio; earlier names were Deelio (deel.io) and The Dealmix per TechCrunch and CB Insights.

rebrands.why: Not stated; TechCrunch says the product was rebuilt during YC

brand_strength.rationale: Three or more names in about a year, a YC directory name that differs from the product name, and no press about the brand itself.

pivots.why: Product rebuilt after joining YC, per TechCrunch

outcome_analysis: The cause of Zipio's shutdown is not public: no post-mortem, acquisition notice or interview was found, only directory labels of Inactive and Dead and a tiny reported seed. The category it served, daily deals, was already crowded with aggregators and faded after 2012, but no source ties the failure to that, so no failure factors are recorded.
notes: Crunchbase and CB Insights both show about $20K total raised, but both are aggregators and are not recorded as a round. Parsers.vc lists the company as Active with last activity 2020, which conflicts with YC and CB Insights. dealupa.com returned HTTP 503 so the site status is unknown. Founding year 2011 inferred from the Deelio launch coverage in Nov 2011 as reported by TechCrunch.
